structured.approach: Attempt 2 fixes every refusal point and rewrites feat.classification.md in full. (1) G2: claims now cite only sources this step accepts, which are feat.intake, feat.prebacklog, record:brief and record:memory. I confirmed with context_list and context_get that org.routing_map and the requirements/ files are not in this step's contract. The routing-map facts were moved out of the claims and into a non-blocking open question (OQ-C2). The repository-to-role routing is now grounded in the bound-repository roles given in the brief. (2) G3: the related-item IDs found by a search outside the contract are no longer stated as claims. They are listed in open question OQ-C3 for the PM to bring into context, so the number '11' no longer appears in any claim. The classification itself is unchanged: the whole entry and each change request were classified against the workbook's Technical Only rule.

claims.text: The entry is classified as a business feature and is not Technical Only, because it gives AP managers a way they can see which overdue invoices belong to vendors that usually pay late. It is linked to roadmap item R-AP-12.

CR-1 (optional paid_date feed column), CR-2 (delays_by_vendor), CR-4 (optional risk argument on build_explanation_request) and CR-7 (end-to-end proof) are Technical Only sub-items. CR-3 (vendor_risk), CR-5 (overdue_with_risk) and CR-6 (renderOverdueRisk) carry the business outcome.

Impacted repositories: ap_pipeline, ap_forecast, ap_aging, ap_portal. ap_pipeline is data engineering (DE), ap_forecast is AI / data science (DS), ap_aging is backend (BE) and ap_portal is frontend (FE).

No duplicates were merged. The intake and the pre-backlog entry describe one ticket and name no other item for the same change. The Pre Backlog sheet and DevOps board were not in context, which feat.prebacklog already raised as OQ-2.
No regulatory source applies, and no conflict was found with D-2026-031, D-2026-044 or D-2026-050.
This agent cannot create the ticket itself because the approved api:github connector allows GET calls only. The classification file is the ticket content.

open_questions: OQ-C1: Is there an approved category taxonomy for the Pre Backlog sheet? 'Business feature (customer-facing enhancement)' with a Technical sub-category per area is proposed.

OQ-C2: The routing map at the path named in the brief lists only ap_aging -> Backend Coding Agent. A feature-level override routes all four repositories (DE, DS, BE, FE) and the end-to-end tests to the Testing Agent. Neither file is a contract item of this step. Please confirm the routing and add the routing map to the contract for later steps.

OQ-C3: Please bring these open requirement items into context and confirm they are related, not duplicates: ZD-48211 and ZD-48501 (same overdue rule in ap_aging as CR-5); ZD-48455 (portal aging table, 'overdue risk' wording); ZD-48470 (same vendor feed and row rejection in ap_pipeline as CR-1, so the order of the two feed changes is needed); PROV-ACME-2026-11 (says to keep the build_explanation_request signature, which CR-4 extends with an optional argument).
OQ-C4: Who creates the new ticket from feat.classification? This agent has no write access to a ticketing system.
OQ-C5: Please confirm the Technical Only split: CR-1, CR-2, CR-4 and CR-7 are Technical Only, and the entry as a whole is not.
structured.summary: Attempt 2 rewrites feat.classification for FEAT-ZD-48600 and now cites only sources in this step's contract. The entry is a business feature for AP managers, linked to R-AP-12, and as a whole it is not Technical Only. CR-1, CR-2, CR-4 and CR-7 are Technical Only sub-items, and CR-3, CR-5 and CR-6 carry the business outcome. Impacted repositories are ap_pipeline, ap_forecast, ap_aging and ap_portal. No duplicates were merged. The full duplicate check against the Pre Backlog sheet and DevOps board, the possibly related items, and the routing-map gap are raised as non-blocking open questions.
